newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CEZ says approves no 1996 dividend.
newsitem.headline: Czech CEZ says approves no 1996 dividend.

text.p: Czech power utility CEZ a.s. approved a zero dividend on 1996 profits at its annual general meeting on Thursday, CEZ spokesman Michal Kacena told Reuters.

"There were two proposals here. The first one of the board of directors, that a two percent dividend would be paid. And the other, by the National Porperty Fund (NPF) that no dividend would be paid," Kacena said.
"The result was that no dividends were approved."
CEZ had planned to pay its first ever dividend on 1996 profits. Originally it said it wanted to pay a three percent dividend but subsequently reduced that proposal to two percent.

But the Industry and Trade Ministry objected to payment of a dividend because of its view that the money should be spent on investment and that it would be politically embarrassing to pay out dividends at a time when prices to households are being raised.
The NPF, the state's main privatisation agency, is CEZ's majority owner, with a 68 percent holding in the company.
